# $\mathrm{SL}_2(F)$ is generated by elementary transvections

Let $F$ be a field. Every matrix of $\mathrm{SL}_2(F)$ is a product of at most four matrices of the
form $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & x \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$ or $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ x & 1 \end{pmatrix}$,
$x \in F$; in particular a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ containing all these matrices contains
$\mathrm{SL}_2(F)$.

Proof. Let $\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}$ have determinant $1$. If $c \ne 0$, it is
$$\begin{pmatrix} 1 & (a-1)/c \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ c & 1 \end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix} 1 & (d-1)/c \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix};$$
if $b \ne 0$, it is
$$\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ (d-1)/b & 1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & b \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ (a-1)/b & 1 \end{pmatrix};$$
and if $b = c = 0$, then $d = 1/a$ and
$$\begin{pmatrix} a & 0 \\ 0 & 1/a \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ (1-a)/a & 1 \end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ a - 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1/a \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}.$$

  $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & * \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$ or $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ * & 1 \end{pmatrix}$"), with the three
  factorizations above.
